title: BeeModel MCP tools
description: The tools BeeModel's MCP server offers (tools/list), each with its JSON Schema input. Published with every release; in 1.x tools are only added. See docs/MCP.md.

tools.name: scene_summary
tools.description: List every object (name, type, location, rotation_deg, scale, selection, mesh size, modifiers, material) and every material with its values.

tools.name: create_primitive
tools.description: Add an object. type: cube, sphere, cylinder, cone, torus, plane, grid, light or camera. Default size: 2 m cube / 1 m radius. Optional name, location, rotation_deg, scale (3 numbers each).

tools.name: set_transform
tools.description: Change an object's location, rotation_deg and/or scale (3 numbers each), or rename it with new_name.

tools.name: select
tools.description: Select objects by name (the last one becomes active). extend keeps the current selection.

tools.name: delete
tools.description: Delete objects by name.

tools.name: run_operator
tools.description: Run any BeeModel operator by id (see console.list_ops), with an optional text argument such as a file path.

tools.name: viewport_capture
tools.description: Look at the scene: a PNG image of the 3D viewport as it is now (area: viewport or window).

tools.name: script_eval
tools.description: Run BeeScript, BeeModel's scripting language, as one undo step; returns what it prints plus the last value. Best for bulk or procedural edits. Syntax: x = 2m; for i in 0..10 { add("cube", "C" + i, i * 2, 0, 0) }; if a > 1 and b { } else { }; while c { }; fn f(a) { return a * 2 }. Units: m cm mm km deg rad (angles are radians, 45deg works). Scene: add(type, [name], [x, y, z]) -> name; move / rotate / scale(name, x, y, z); scale(name, s); get(name, prop) and set(name, prop, v) with prop x y z rx ry rz sx sy sz; select(names...); delete(names...); rename(old, new); exists(name); count(); name(i); active(); op(id, [arg]). Also print(...), str, num, len, sin, cos, tan, sqrt, abs, floor, round, min, max, pow, atan2, deg, rad, rand, seed, pi.

tools.name: ui_tree
tools.description: List the widgets on screen this frame (buttons, fields, toggles, lists, sections) with their name, sub index, kind, rectangle in window pixels, label and value. Use it to find what the user sees and where to click.

tools.name: undo
tools.description: Undo the last change.

tools.name: redo
tools.description: Redo the last undone change.

tools.name: node_types
tools.description: The geometry node catalogue: every type with its inputs (slots 1-3, kinds, defaults), values (slots 4-7, kinds, choices, defaults) and outputs, and how the tree.* operators use them.

tools.name: describe_graph
tools.description: A geometry node tree as JSON: its nodes (type, links into each input as node + output, constants, values, place) - or every tree when no name is given; also the open proposal's state.

tools.name: propose_begin
tools.description: Open a proposal: the changes until the user accepts or reverts are one undo step. Then build with the tree.* operators or script_eval, and call propose_end.

title.description: what it does, shown to the user

tools.name: propose_end
tools.description: Show the open proposal to the user: a banner in the viewport to Accept (keep it) or Revert (take it all back).

tools.name: proposal_status
tools.description: The proposal's state: none, building, waiting for the user, accepted or reverted.

tools.name: material_node_types
tools.description: The material node catalogue (the node editor's): every type with its inputs (slots 1-3, kinds, defaults), values (slots 4-7, kinds, choices, defaults) and outputs, and how material_graph_set and BeeScript use them.

tools.name: material_graph
tools.description: A material's node graph as JSON: nodes (type, values, inputs as constants or links {link: node, output}, pos, parameter name) and the Material Output's sockets.

tools.name: material_graph_set
tools.description: Replace a material's node graph (the material is made when missing) from the JSON material_graph returns: graph = {nodes: [...], sockets: {...}}. Nodes are numbered from 1 in order. One undo step.

tools.name: reference_view
tools.description: Look at a reference image (a drawing or photo to model over, object.add_references): its picture as a PNG, at most 1024 px (thin lines kept), and what it is: its size in pixels, the metres a pixel is, how it stands and its folder. x0 y0 x1 y1 (its pixels; 0,0 its top-left) show a part of it closer, to read a pixel exactly for object.reference_pin.
